subject: A finished native Chalk Flower style and paper skin for Terminal Delight, with captures and validation.
reader: Parker requested this implementation from a paper-and-chalk concept, knows Terminal Delight, and wants to see what shipped and what was verified.

sections.heading: Chalk Flower, in the terminal
sections.text:
The paper workshop is now a native style and skin. Choose chalk light or chalk dark in the appearance picker. Both request the paper skin when Skin follows the theme; Paper can also sit over your current palette. 
 Native captures verified Both terminal cores pass Caveat UI · JetBrains Mono terminal

sections.heading: Paper around the work
sections.text:
The frame carries pigment grain. Buttons are pale offcuts with an irregular edge, a small shadow and an accent stamp. The terminal keeps a flat reading surface and its monospace font. 01 · Chalk light 
 The material surrounds the text without deforming the glyphs. Native release capture on this laptop. The transcript is fixed sample output; it is separate from the real test results below.

sections.heading: The same stock on slate
sections.text:
Dark mode uses the same controls and layout, with chalk ink on charcoal paper. Sticky notes keep their editing, pin and peel gestures, and gain fibres, a tape strip and a small flower on the curl. 02 · Chalk dark 
 The paper skin follows the palette instead of carrying a second fixed set of colours. Native capture after closing and reopening the test window; the style and note persisted.

sections.heading: What the native checks found
sections.text:
The new styles pass the existing contrast and status-colour checks under every built-in skin. The paper texture is one cached image, and edge detail stays bounded. Changing skin, opening the Workbench and restoring the window all worked in the isolated native fixture. 
 | 
 | Check | Result 
 | Rio terminal core + integration suites | 2,489 passed; 9 ignored 
 | Alacritty terminal core + integration suites | 2,442 passed; 9 ignored 
 | Strict Clippy, formatting and release build | Passed 
 | Light small-print contrast | 5.01:1 on the sheet; 4.59:1 on the frame 
 | Dark small-print contrast | 5.45:1 on the sheet; 4.66:1 on the frame 
 | Window restart | Both styles returned with Paper and their saved note 

The texture adds drawing cost. These are four alternating five-second samples for each workload, from the same native window: 
 | 
 | Terminal output | Default skin | Paper skin 
 | Idle · first pair | 2.6% of one CPU core | 2.6% 
 | Idle · second pair | 2.2% | 3.0% 
 | 20 Hz · first pair | 17.0% | 20.2% 
 | 20 Hz · second pair | 15.4% | 20.4% 
Measured on an NVIDIA RTX 3080 Laptop system, with two panes visible, one sticky note and a third pane behind another tab. Other builds were running on the machine. These short samples establish this fixture’s cost; they do not measure 60 fps frame pacing.

sections.heading: Keep shaping the materials
sections.text:
You can annotate either native capture or these two choices, then save this file with your notes. 

 Paper weight and grain 
Current treatment: quiet gesso inside, pigment on the frame, pale controls with a small accent stamp. 
 The sticky-note offcuts 
Current treatment: matching paper, a tape strip and a pressed-flower mark. Accent and muted note colours remain available. 
 Source, provenance and verification files 
The palette and Caveat handwriting follow Parker’s existing Chalk theme in parkerbrown-dev/app/globals.css and its light/dark pair in next-run/lib/theme/chalk.ts . The stacked-paper reference guides the edges and shadows. The implementation branch contains the renderer, skin, two styles and tests. 
 app/src/paper.rs owns the shared grain and bounded outline. app/src/skin.rs owns the material and UI font; the terminal font remains on its existing path. The already bundled Caveat font is SIL OFL. No new dependency or host-protocol change was required. 
Full test logs, native fixture, restart receipts and raw performance samples accompany the report in reports/2026-10-19-chalk-flower-evidence/ . Native windows ran on isolated hidden workspaces; the working session was untouched during verification.
